meta.purpose: Input-test spec for the Fluid-UI hotkey/wheel/pointer surface. Every entry verified against handler source; file:line refs are the proof.

sources.reference_sheet: index.html:1049-1155 (F1 modal; marketing copy, not authority)
sources.typing_guard: js/01a-param-registry.js:363-374 (window.__isTypingTarget: textarea/select/contenteditable/text-like input types block; range/checkbox/color inputs do NOT block)

synthesis.keyboard: All keyboard handlers read only e.key/e.code/modifiers/e.repeat/e.target — synthetic (untrusted) KeyboardEvent dispatched on document works for every binding. CDP Input.dispatchKeyEvent also works. Dispatch on document so e.target=document (never a typing target).
synthesis.wheel: Dispatch WheelEvent on #canvas-area (or #canvas, it bubbles) with {deltaY, bubbles:true, cancelable:true, clientX/clientY over the canvas} plus modifier flags. Handler is bubble-phase on #canvas-area (js/05h-slider-bindings.js:311). Zoom Mode's capture-phase handler intercepts first when active (js/35-zoom-view.js:168-180) — keep zoomMode off.
synthesis.pointer: Real strokes: CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent (mousePressed/mouseMoved/mouseReleased, button 'left') over the canvas — Chromium synthesizes trusted PointerEvents with pointerType 'mouse'. Synthetic PointerEvent via dispatchEvent also drives the state machine (handlers never check isTrusted); getCoalescedEvents is absent on synthetic events and the handler falls back to a single sample (js/05d-input-replay.js:635-643).
synthesis.bare_globals: isPaused, recEnabled, recLayers, recActiveLayerId, recCountdownActive, recIsPlayingAll, currentPaletteIndex, paletteStepIndex, savedColors, splatOutActive, bordersLocked are top-level let/const in classic scripts — NOT window properties, but readable by bare identifier in CDP Runtime.evaluate (shared global lexical scope). window.pointer, window.animationMultiplier, window.__fluidFrozen, window.config, window.recIsEnabled(), window.recGetActiveLayerId(), window.recGetLayersSnapshot(), window.ZoomView, window.fluidExport, window.mutationEngine ARE on window.
